title: Recomputing the Excess in a Closing and Funding Prepaid Interest Dispute
content:
**Formal clause.** A prepaid interest dispute decision decides a borrower's pending per diem overcharge dispute on a funded Closing and Funding closing by recomputing what the disputed charge still holds. In the standard recompute, the disputed charge is the closing's latest prepaid interest charge (the charge entry whose period starts latest). In the standard recompute, the standing days are every day of the disputed charge. The excess is the standing days times the refund per standing day, rounded half up to the cent. In the standard recompute, the refund per standing day is zero. In the standard recompute, the excess carries no interest. The refund is the excess plus any interest it carries.

**Filing decided.** The filing the recompute decides is the closing's latest per diem overcharge filing still marked pending; where none is pending nothing is decided, and a filing that a decision record already names is not decided again, nothing further being refunded for it.

**Outcome.** A decision with a refund above zero is issued as a refund with the refund as its amount; a decision with nothing to refund is denied as correct as charged with an amount of zero.

## Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| disputed charge | 3 through 28 February, 26 days, daily amount 74.10 |
| refund per standing day | zero in the standard recompute |

- Standing days: every day of the charge, 26.
- Excess: 26 times zero is 0.00; no interest is carried.
- Decision: nothing to refund, so denied as correct as charged with an amount of 0.00.

The arithmetic of the excess with a nonzero figure, for illustration only: 26 standing days at 1.15 a day is 29.90.

| Situation | Decision |
|---|---|
| the latest pending per diem overcharge filing is already named by a decision record | not decided again; nothing further refunded |
| no per diem overcharge filing is pending | nothing is decided |
